overview_pre: **Counselling level only**: what patients ask about toxin and fillers, UK regulation and red flags. No injection technique, doses or units.
kf: Ageing is **intrinsic** (time, genes) and **extrinsic** (UV, smoking): volume loss, bone remodelling, elastosis, wrinkles.
**Dynamic lines** come from muscle movement; **static lines** stay at rest.
Botulinum toxin softens dynamic lines; it **doesn't lift sagging skin or replace volume**.
Toxin is **prescription-only**; GPhC: prescribers must assess **face to face**. Illegal for under-18s cosmetically (2021 Act).
Filler red flags: **vascular occlusion** (pain, blanching, mottling, visual change) is an emergency.
myths: **"Fillers and toxin are the same"**: toxin relaxes muscle; fillers add volume.
patho_lead: Botulinum toxin **stops nerves signalling to muscle** for a few months.

mech.t: Toxin is taken up into the motor nerve terminal.
It cuts SNAP-25, so acetylcholine vesicles can't release.
The injected muscle weakens and dynamic lines soften.
New nerve sprouts restore function over about 3–4 months.

comp: Bruising, headache, eyelid ptosis, asymmetry; filler: lumps, infection, vascular occlusion, blindness (rare).
prog: Effects wear off; repeat treatment needed.
